title: Gear fit: who an item is built for
about: The rules behind wow-stats' gear fit labels (wowstats/gearfit.py): which stats each role uses, armour types, Forever's spell power on gear, and group-loot custom. Written in our own words, each with two or more sources.

statements.title: Healing power does nothing for a class without heals
statements.text: Warriors, rogues, mages, warlocks and hunters have no healing spells of their own, so an item's healing line does nothing for them. Its spell damage, when it has some, still counts for the casters.

statements.title: Hybrids heal themselves while levelling
statements.text: A priest, druid, shaman or paladin levelling in a damage or tank spec still heals between pulls, so healing power is worth something to them while levelling. It matters less once the spec's 31-point talent changes how it plays: Shadowform allows every spell but the healing ones.

statements.title: A tree's 31-point talent comes at 40 at the earliest
statements.text: Talent points come one a level from 10, so 31 points in one tree, its last talent, come at level 40 at the earliest. Shadow priest guides place Shadowform between 40 and 42, depending on the points spent elsewhere.

statements.title: Healing gear also carries spell damage
statements.text: In Forever, gear with bonus healing also gets some spell damage, so healers can quest with it. In the item tables wow-stats reads, a healing item's damage value is about a third of its healing value (median 3.0 to 1 over 210 items); items with one value for both are the caster pieces.

statements.title: Spell power on gear from level 10
statements.text: Forever puts spell power on gear from about level 10, first on weapons, and lowered spells' base damage to match: a caster's weapon and gear matter while levelling, as weapons do for a rogue.

statements.title: Warriors and rogues have no mana
statements.text: Warriors and rogues use rage and energy: Intellect, Spirit and mana regeneration on gear do nothing for them, and no stat priority for them lists those stats.

statements.title: Attack power is for weapon attacks
statements.text: Attack power raises weapon and physical ability damage, not spells: casters and healers get nothing from it. Retribution paladins and Enhancement shamans fight with weapons and use it.

statements.title: Ranged attack power is for hunters
statements.text: Ranged attack power only raises bow, gun and crossbow damage (not wands). Hunters use it; for warriors and rogues it only touches a throw or a shot now and then.

statements.title: Armour types and the level 40 step
statements.text: Mages, priests and warlocks wear cloth only; rogues and druids leather; hunters and shamans leather, then mail from 40; warriors and paladins mail, then plate from 40. A lower type still works: warrior guides say better stats beat the armour type.

statements.title: Gear is built per role
statements.text: Items are made for a role by their stats: defense, dodge, parry and block for tanks; healing power, Intellect, Spirit and mana regen for healers; spell damage, spell hit and Intellect for damage casters; Strength, Agility, attack power, hit and crit for weapon fighters. Each spec's stat priority says which it uses.

statements.title: Who rolls first in a group
statements.text: Most groups let the player whose main spec the item is built for roll first, and many also favour the class for which it is the best armour type (mail for a hunter or shaman over a rogue). Asking the group first is the usual courtesy; it's a custom, not a game rule.

open_questions.text: A second source for pure spell-damage cloth being scarce while levelling in Forever, and for Blizzard acknowledging it: none found yet (one community thread only).
